unitKey: 2Solid, liquid, gas states and changes of stateChemistry

questions.question: What is the temperature at which pure water both boils and condenses?
What state of matter is steam?
options: Solid state
Liquid state
Gas state
Plasma state

questions.question: How do particles change their arrangement when a substance is condensed?
options: They move further apart
They move closer together
They stop moving completely
They increase in size

questions.question: What change occurs when you open the air hole of a Bunsen burner?
options: The flame turns blue, hotter, and cleaner
The flame turns orange and produces soot
The flame immediately goes out
The flame gets larger without changing color

questions.question: Which action controls the size of a Bunsen burner flame?
options: Opening or closing the collar
Adjusting the gas tap
Moving the chimney up and down
Changing the rubber tubing

questions.question: What is the correct safety technique for carrying a lit splint?
options: Pointing straight up above your head
Angled slightly downwards and shielded with your other hand
Held horizontally as fast as possible
Pointing straight down towards your feet

questions.question: Which state of matter has the least energy, and which has the most energy?
options: Solid has the least energy, gas has the most energy
Gas has the least energy, liquid has the most energy
Liquid has the least energy, solid has the most energy
Solid has the least energy, liquid has the most energy

questions.question: At what temperatures can a liquid undergo evaporation?
options: Only at its boiling point
Only at temperatures above its boiling point
At temperatures below its boiling point
Only when it is frozen

questions.question: How does increasing the temperature of water affect its rate of evaporation?
options: The hotter the water, the more slowly it evaporates
The hotter the water, the more quickly it evaporates
Temperature has no effect on evaporation rate
Water stops evaporating when heated

questions.question: What state change occurs when a substance melts?
options: Liquid state to solid state
Gas state to liquid state
Solid state to liquid state
Liquid state to gas state

questions.question: How do the melting point and freezing point of a pure substance compare?
options: The melting point is always higher than the freezing point
The freezing point is always higher than the melting point
They are the exact same temperature
They change depending on the container size

questions.question: Why do particles in a solid remain in fixed positions?
options: Forces of attraction hold them in fixed positions
They are glued to each other permanently
They have too much energy to move around
Air pressure pushes them together from outside

questions.question: What effect do stronger forces of attraction between particles have on a substance's melting point?
options: The melting point becomes lower
The melting point stays at 0°C
The melting point becomes higher
The substance cannot melt at all

questions.question: What is the approximate temperature of a healthy human body?
options: 0ºC
20ºC
37ºC
100ºC

questions.question: Why must the bulb of a liquid thermometer be handled carefully?
options: It contains toxic gas under high pressure
It is made of very thin, delicate glass
It dissolves when touched by hands
It loses its temperature reading instantly

questions.question: Which set of properties describes a substance in the gas state?
options: Has a fixed shape and cannot be compressed
Can flow, fills the whole container, and can be compressed
Fills the shape of its container and cannot be compressed
Does not flow and has a fixed volume

questions.question: Why can particles in a gas move completely free of one another?
options: They have enough energy to break free of attractive forces
They are connected by soft springs
They are repelled by magnetic forces
They are too large to attract each other

questions.question: What is present in the spaces between particles in a gas?
options: Air
Liquid droplets
Nothing at all
Tiny dust particles

questions.question: Which properties are characteristic of the solid state?
options: Fixed shape, does not flow, and cannot be compressed
Fills the whole container, flows, and can be compressed
Fills the shape of its container, flows, and can be compressed
No fixed shape, flows easily, and cannot be compressed

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a liquid's properties?
options: It has a fixed shape and can be compressed easily
It can flow, fills the shape of its container, and cannot be compressed
It fills the whole volume of any container and can be compressed
It cannot flow and has a fixed shape
